mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Sport 3.6 TDV8 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Range Rover Sport 3.6 TDV8 (368DT) engine typically costs between £7,000 and £10,500 for supply only, while reconditioned units start from £5,500.

historyTimeline.h2: Range Rover Sport 3.6 TDV8 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 3.6 TDV8 was introduced to the L320 Range Rover Sport in 2006, it marked the arrival of a powerful, twin-turbocharged V8 diesel that offered immense torque and refined performance, bridging the gap between the 2.7 TDV6 and the later 4.4 SDV8.

milestones.description: 368DT (3.6L TDV8), 272hp, introduced to the L320 Range Rover Sport, featuring twin turbochargers, a robust cast-iron block, and advanced common-rail injection.
End of 3.6 TDV8 production in the L320 generation, replaced by the 4.4 SDV8 (448DT) in the subsequent L494 generation.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Range Rover Sport 3.6 TDV8 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover Sport 3.6 TDV8 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Range Rover Sport 3.6 TDV8 (368DT) delivers formidable V8 torque, but early L320 units are susceptible to specific wear points, notably timing chain and crankshaft issues. Rebuilt engines sourced through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Range Rover Sport 3.6 TDV8 368DT Suffers Premature Wear
problems.rootCause: Early-production timing chain tensioners are prone to premature wear, leading to chain rattle on cold starts and potential catastrophic valve-to-piston contact if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing timing chains, guides, and upgraded tensioners before failure occurs.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if caught early (audible rattle but no running issues).

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if the chain has already jumped or engine has suffered valve damage.

problems.recommendation: For early signs of timing chain rattle or turbo actuator issues, targeted specialist repair is highly cost-effective. However, if the 368DT has suffered catastrophic crankshaft fracture or severe internal wear, a full rebuilt engine with upgraded tensioners and heavy-duty bearings offers the best long-term reliability and protects your investment.

problems.h4: Crankshaft Fracture & Turbo Actuator Failure - Why the Range Rover Sport 3.6 TDV8 368DT Loses Power
problems.rootCause: The 3.6 TDV8 shares design similarities with the 2.7 TDV6, making it susceptible to crankshaft stress under high load, compounded by turbo actuator corrosion and failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Repair or replacement of damaged wiring harness sections and boost actuator unit.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if actuator is still functional and only wiring corroded.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Required if crankshaft has fractured or engine has seized.
